desc:
Given an integer array nums and two bounds lo ≤ hi, return the number of non-empty contiguous subarrays whose maximum element lies between lo and hi inclusive.

nums = [2, 1, 4, 3], lo = 2, hi = 3
qualifying: [2], [2, 1], [3]
result = 3
hints: The maximum of a subarray is at most hi exactly when every element is at most hi.
Count subarrays whose maximum is at most x: these are the subarrays that lie inside a run of consecutive elements that are all at most x.
The answer is atMost(hi) - atMost(lo - 1). A run of length L contributes L(L+1)/2 to atMost; you can also count by right end, adding the current run length.
editorial: Let atMost(x) be the number of subarrays whose maximum is at most x. Such a subarray contains only elements ≤ x, so it lies inside a maximal run of such elements. Scanning left to right, keep the length of the current run (reset to 0 at an element greater than x) and add it to the total at every position: that counts the subarrays ending there.

A subarray has its maximum in [lo, hi] iff its maximum is at most hi but not at most lo - 1, so the answer is atMost(hi) - atMost(lo - 1). Both passes are linear: O(n) time and O(1) space. Counting directly ("the maximum is at least lo") would need extra bookkeeping about the last big element; the difference form avoids it.
